author: nero_eth
content:
There's some time between the bid selected and the attestation deadline in which unbundling risk is high but not mev-stealing by parsing state diffs.
Independently, even if builders treat bal and payload exactly the same (which makes not much sense) the eip would still help by splitting one potentially huge object into two on the wire.
By setting the BAL availability deadline 1s earlier than the payload deadline, you'd guarantee 1 more second of useful EL work in worst-cases.

author: nero_eth
content: We don't ask builders to reveal the BAL before bidding but only after. Then the proposer can potentially equivovate (and get slashed) but stealing mev is much much less profit than unbundling. We're talking about a few hundret bucks vs millions of dollars. So, there basically no risk in releasing early.

author: potuz
content: BTW, I strongly support erasure coding for the whole envelope that is also proposed for Hegota and will also provide the same benefit of faster propagation. I just dispute that we can get BALs before the rest and I believe erasure coding gives us a much better return for propagation.

author: nero_eth
content:
With a 1s earlier deadline you'd enforce it, so at least in the worst case, you'd get the BAL earlier. And it's safe bc in the worst case builder wait until the attestation deadline for publishing the payload but wouldn't need to wait that long for the BAL (seeing the bid in the block is enough).
Erasure encoding of the two objects should be done independently.

author: potuz
content: we can't be too frugal with deadline enforcing of things as that can eventually lead to split views IMO, it also complicates the builder and CL sides as well. Same for erasure coding, having different and independent paths of dissemination for both of these objects seems to me contraproducent and overkill.

author: nero_eth
content:
I think it's fine as long as we stay conservative with buffers. E.g. we allow 6s for the payload knowing 99.99% of the payloads are seen multiple seconds earlier. The same would apply to the BAL.
Afterall, BAL and payload are very different things and in the future, thinking of zkEVMs, we might have parties that are only interested in the BAL and not in the payload, and those would like a state diff + prove, not downloading the growing payload.

author: nero_eth
content: Another cartegory are focil includers who may want to download the BAL as early in the slot as possible, apply it to their state and then build higher qulity ILs. The EIP provides them 1 additional second in the worst-case, which comes very handy (and advancing the state by the current payload is great for focil but also halfway through the post-state root calculation).

author: nero_eth
content: Generally agree that deadlines should be used carefully. To me it does feel natural though to separate things into block <> payload <> state diff (bal) <> proof, in the future.

author: 0w3n6325
content: Is the benefit mostly network propagation time savings or the processing that happens when the BAL arrives at the EL? If it’s the former I think builders would be willing to encrypt the BAL, gossip early, and then put the key in the payload?
